question:
Two different positions of the same dice marked with the numbers I, II, III, IV, V and VI are shown.

Select the number that will be on the face opposite to the face having the number 'IV'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea1a9ef5c57fdf4e085921edbd3eb7d9d42029629221850c7bcec544f474b797.png]
solution:
For this question, the relation is given below :-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f6c4cf8e8694448b73c7f5aa737e695992e638a9331c01755bdb3f4bee8ceed.png] 

Logic : **If two dice have the same two face value in the given image then the third number is opposite to each other.**

In first dice and second dice.

Roman numbers I and III are common.

So, **Roman number IV is opposite to VI.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"VI".**
